quote:
Started building [asmi](https://asmiai.com/) because I kept procrastinating on calls (dentist, insurance, bookings). The hypothesis: if an AI could just do them for me over SMS, I'd actually get them done.

Surprising pivot 3 weeks in: the most common use case isn't phone calls. It's navigating terrible multi-step websites. People will text an agent to handle a 7-step online form faster than they'd open the tab.

Building in SMS keeps the friction near zero. No app to open, no new interface to learn. Just text a contact and the task is done.

Try it: [https://asmi-ai.link/imsg](https://asmi-ai.link/imsg)

Curious if other builders have noticed this pattern: the actual use case being different from the intended one?
author: u/Fit-Cup-4468
notes: founder: pivot to navigating bad websites via SMS

quote:
[Asmi](https://asmiai.com/) is an AI personal assistant you access over iMessage or WhatsApp - no app to install.

You give it a task over a quick message, a voice note, or a call. It handles it happily.

That might mean browsing the web to research and compare options, booking a reservation or appointment on a website, adding groceries to a cart and sending you a ready-to-checkout link, making an outbound phone call on your behalf, sending an email, or coordinating something across multiple steps.

A few things we would like to being upfront about:

We're early. About 1000 beta users right now. Things break. Some tasks work better than others. We're actively figuring out where Asmi is most useful and where it falls short.

We're not a calling app. Calling is one thing Asmi can do. The broader vision is an assistant that handles real-world tasks across whatever surface makes sense - web, phone, email, chat.

We're consumer-focused. Personal life tasks - travel, groceries, appointments, reservations, home services, admin. Not work. Not B2B.

If you're here, you're probably curious or already in beta. Either way - ask questions, share what you've tried, tell us what broke. That's gen
